name: Sign in with Apple and Credential Manager
plain: Account sign in that can hide the real email behind a relay address.
meaning: Apple required it where other social logins existed until January 2024. Android uses Credential Manager.

android.permission: None; Credential Manager with Google ID, passkeys, passwords
android.note: Hide My Email equivalent is Google's limited scope

ios.prompt_ui: Sign in with Apple sheet with Hide My Email
ios.revocation: Settings > Apple Account > Sign in with Apple
ios.note: Returns stable user id; email may be a relay address; name only on first sign in

limits.headline: Can sign you in with Apple and hide your real email if you choose
limits.user_action: You tap Sign in with Apple and choose Share or Hide My Email
can: Create an account using your Apple ID with Face ID or Touch ID
Get a steady user ID for your account
Receive a private relay email instead of your real one
Learn your name on the first sign in only
cannot: See your real email when you pick Hide My Email
Get your name again on later sign ins
Use your sign in on another developer's app
limits.reach_label: Only what you choose to share
limits.differs: Apple offers a Hide My Email relay. On Android, Credential Manager offers Google, passkeys and passwords with a more limited scope.

story.what_it_is: You sign in with your Apple account and can hide your real email address.

marketing.name: Sign in with Apple
marketing.pitch: A private, simple way to sign in with Face ID, with the option to hide your email address.

marketing.name: Credential Manager
marketing.pitch: Android's single sign in sheet for passwords, passkeys and federated sign in options.

story.for_you: You see a black Apple button, tap it and confirm with Face ID. You can pick Hide My Email, so the app gets a random address that forwards to your real inbox. You can switch it off later.
story.for_makers: Makers get a fast sign up with a verified account, which means more finished sign ups. If you hide your email, they cannot easily link you to other data. It also means the maker must send mail to the relay and cannot simply sell your address.

use_cases.example: A store account starts with one tap and a forwarding email, so promo mail never hits your main inbox.
A social app creates your profile from your Apple name without asking you to type it.
A game ties your save file to your Apple account so it restores on a new iPhone.
A news app uses a relay email so it can send newsletters, and you can turn them off at the source.
A dating app signs you up faster and sees only the name you choose to share.
A marketer finds relay emails harder to match across companies, which weakens cross app tracking.

risks: Lock in to an Apple account
story.android_note: Android apps show a Credential Manager sheet and may offer Sign in with Apple through the web.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps get the native Apple button, with a required relay email option when it is used.

technical_bounds: Name and email are delivered once
Relay email forwards only if the developer registers sending domains

history.change: Guideline 4.8 revised to allow any privacy preserving login
Any equivalent privacy-focused login service may satisfy 4.8
Account deletion rule 5.1.1(v) requires token revocation
Sign in with Apple introduced; required by 4.8 if other social login is offered
